sub: Named after “set out in detail” (fuṣṣilat) in ayah 3; also called Ḥā Mīm as-Sajdah
theme: The Quraysh refused even to listen to the Qurʾan. The surah answers that stubborn rejection with creation, the fate of ʿĀd and Thamūd, and the Day their own skins testify, and tells believers to answer evil with good.
story: Revealed in Makkah, after Ḥamzah had accepted Islam, when the Muslims were growing. ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, a Quraysh chief, went to the Prophet ﷺ with offers: wealth, leadership, kingship, or doctors if a jinn had taken hold of him.

The Prophet ﷺ heard him out, then recited this surah. In one report he reached the prostration at ayah 38 and prostrated; in another, ʿUtbah put his hand over his mouth at ayah 13, begging him by kinship to stop.

ʿUtbah returned with his face changed: “It is not poetry, sorcery or soothsaying. Leave him alone.” The chiefs said he had been bewitched. The surah ignores the offers and answers the real issue: their refusal to listen.

sections.title: A detailed Arabic Qurʾan meets closed hearts; the call is one God
sections.meaning: A Book from the Most Merciful, detailed and in Arabic, bringing good news and warning. Most turn away: “Our hearts are covered, our ears deaf.” The Prophet ﷺ says he is only a man: your God is One, so go straight to Him. Woe to idolaters; believers get an endless reward.
points: Ḥā Mīm; a detailed Arabic Book from the Most Merciful
Good news and warning, yet they say: hearts covered, ears deaf
Only a man; your God is One; woe to idolaters without zakah
Believers who do good get a reward that never stops
sections.matters: It sets up the whole surah: a clear Book, and people who refuse even to hear it. The reply is humble, not angry. The Prophet ﷺ claims nothing but revelation, and simply calls them back to one God and forgiveness.
sections.story: These opening ayat were among those recited to ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah after he offered the Prophet ﷺ wealth and power. Their claim “our hearts are covered” was the Quraysh’s way of mocking and refusing to listen.
explained: Fuṣṣilat āyātuhu: its ayat are set out in detail, subject by subject, in clear Arabic, so people who want to understand can. It gives good news to believers and warns deniers. But most turned away and would not truly listen.

They mocked: our hearts are in akinnah (coverings), our ears are heavy, a screen divides us, so do your work and we will do ours. The Prophet ﷺ answers humbly: I am a man like you, given revelation. Go straight to the One God and seek His forgiveness. Woe to the idolaters; the believers’ reward never ends.
teaches: The Qurʾan was made clear; the barrier is a heart that refuses to listen.
Answer mockery with humility, not insult.
Go straight to Allah, and seek forgiveness for the slips along the way.
Faith shows itself in purifying the soul and giving to others.
sections.hook: Ḥā Mīm opens it, as it opens surahs 40 and 42. Ayah 5 names three barriers in a row: hearts (akinnah), ears (waqr), a screen (ḥijāb). Ayah 6 answers with “Say”.

sections.title: Denying the Creator of earth and heavens invites ʿĀd and Thamūd’s fate
sections.meaning: How can you deny the One who made the earth in two days, set mountains, blessings and provision on it, then formed the smoke into seven heavens in two days? If they still turn away, warn them of a blast like the one that struck ʿĀd and Thamūd. The believers were saved.
points: You deny the One who made the earth in two days?
Mountains, blessing and provision: four days in all
Sky and earth come willingly; seven heavens, stars as lamps
Warned of a blast like ʿĀd and Thamūd’s; they wanted angels
ʿĀd: “Who is stronger than us?” A screaming wind
Thamūd chose blindness over guidance; the believers were saved
sections.matters: Section 1 said the Qurʾan is clear. This section gives the proof and the warning: the Creator of everything needs no partner, and nations that trusted their strength and rejected their messengers were wiped out, while believers were saved.
sections.story: Reportedly, when the Prophet ﷺ reached ayah 13 while reciting to ʿUtbah, ʿUtbah put his hand over his mouth and begged him by kinship to stop. He later told the Quraysh: “You know he never lies, and I feared punishment would fall on you.”
explained: Allah made the earth in two days, then set firm mountains on it, blessed it and measured out its provisions, making four days in all, an exact answer for anyone asking. Then He turned to the sky, which was smoke, and told sky and earth: come, willingly or not. They said: we come willingly.

He completed seven heavens in two more days and decorated the nearest with stars, for beauty and protection from devils. So if they turn away, warn them. Messengers came to ʿĀd and Thamūd; they wanted angels. ʿĀd boasted of strength and a howling wind humbled them. Thamūd preferred blindness to guidance and a humiliating blast seized them.
teaches: The One who made the heavens and earth has no equal, so worship Him alone.
Allah could create in a moment, yet He created in stages, with wisdom.
Strength and power protect no one from Allah.
Being shown guidance is not the same as taking it.
Allah saves those who believe and guard themselves against sin.
sections.hook: It starts at the ۞ mark (ayah 9) with “Say”. The days run two (9), four (10), two (12). Then a pair: “As for ʿĀd” (15), “As for Thamūd” (17).

sections.title: Allah’s enemies: skins testify, they shouted down the Qurʾan, the Fire awaits
sections.meaning: Allah’s enemies are driven to the Fire, and their ears, eyes and skins testify against them. They thought Allah didn’t know much of what they did, and that thought ruined them. Devilish companions made sin look good. They told each other to drown out the Qurʾan; now they beg to trample those who misled them.
points: Allah’s enemies driven to the Fire; ears, eyes, skins testify
“Why testify against us?” “Allah made us speak”
You didn’t hide, thinking Allah didn’t know; that thought ruined you
Patience won’t help; companions made their sins look attractive
“Don’t listen, make noise”: the Fire is their eternal home
“Show us who misled us, so we trample them”
sections.matters: Section 2 showed punishment in this world; this section shows the next. Nothing is hidden: the body itself becomes a witness. It also exposes the Quraysh’s tactic of shouting over the Qurʾan so no one could hear it, and shows where following misleaders ends.
sections.story: Reportedly, three men sat by the Kaʿbah, from Quraysh and Thaqīf. One asked whether Allah hears them; another said only if they spoke loudly. When the Prophet ﷺ was told, ayat 22–23 were revealed. Abū Jahl also had his men shout over the recitation (26).
explained: The enemies of Allah are herded to the Fire, the front held back until the rest catch up. At its edge, their ears, eyes and skins testify to everything they did. They protest to their skins, which answer: Allah, who makes everything speak, made us speak. He created you first, and to Him you return.

You never hid your sins from your limbs; you assumed Allah didn’t know much of it, and that bad thought about your Lord destroyed you. Devilish companions made this world look beautiful and the Hereafter seem unreal. The deniers said: don’t listen, make noise. In the Fire, the followers beg to crush their misleaders, jinn and human, underfoot.
teaches: You can hide from people, but not from your own limbs.
Assuming Allah doesn’t see is a bad thought about Him that leads to ruin.
Listen quietly when the Qurʾan is recited; shouting it down is the deniers’ way.
Choose your companions: bad ones make sin look beautiful.
Misleaders and their followers will turn on each other.
sections.hook: “Enemies of Allah” (aʿdāʾ Allāh) appears at 19 and 28. The same three witnesses, ears, eyes, skins, come in 20 and 22. The ۞ mark falls at ayah 25.

sections.title: Angels reassure the steadfast; callers to Allah answer evil with good
sections.meaning: Those who say “Our Lord is Allah” and stay firm hear the angels: don’t fear, don’t grieve, Paradise is yours. No speech beats calling to Allah while doing good. Answer evil with what is better, and an enemy becomes a close friend. Against Satan’s whispers, seek refuge in Allah.
points: “Our Lord is Allah”, then steadfast: angels say don’t fear, don’t grieve
Your allies here and hereafter; whatever you wish, a welcome gift
Best speech: calling to Allah, doing good, “I am a Muslim”
Repel evil with better; only the patient and fortunate manage it
When Satan nudges you, seek refuge in Allah
sections.matters: The surah turns from deniers to believers. It gave the weak, persecuted Muslims of Makkah two things: angels on their side in this life and the next, and a method for their mission, which is patient good character, not revenge.
sections.story: No specific incident for the passage as a whole. Reports link single ayat to people: ayah 30 to Abū Bakr, ayah 33 to the Prophet ﷺ or those who call the adhān, and ayah 34 to Abū Sufyān.
explained: Istiqāmah: saying “Our Lord is Allah” and then holding firm, not adding partners, doing what He commands and avoiding what He forbids. Angels descend on such people, at death, in the grave and at the resurrection: don’t fear what’s ahead, don’t grieve for what you leave behind. We were your allies in this life and will be in the next.

Paradise is a welcome gift (nuzul) from the Forgiving, the Merciful. No one’s words are better than one who calls to Allah and lives it. Good and evil are not equal: repel wrong with what is better, and your enemy becomes like a close friend. Only the patient reach this. When Satan stirs you to retaliate, seek refuge in Allah.
teaches: Say “My Lord is Allah”, then stay firm on it.
Call others only to what you practise yourself.
Treating a wrongdoer well can turn an enemy into a friend.
Patience with anger, forbearance with ignorance, forgiveness for harm.
When anger pushes you to hit back, seek refuge in Allah.
sections.hook: Page 480 begins at ayah 30. Devil companions, quranāʾ (25), are answered by angel allies, awliyāʾ (31). Wa mā yulaqqāhā illā comes twice in ayah 35.

sections.title: Prostrate to Allah, not sun or moon; deniers reject His guarded Book
sections.meaning: Sun and moon are His signs: prostrate to their Creator, as the angels tirelessly do. Rain reviving dead earth shows He will revive the dead. Those who twist His ayat can’t hide. Falsehood can’t reach the Qurʾan; it heals believers, while deniers are deaf to it. Mūsā’s Book was disputed too.
points: Don’t prostrate to sun or moon; angels glorify Him tirelessly
Dead earth stirs with rain: its Reviver revives the dead
Those who twist Our ayat aren’t hidden; do what you like
A mighty Book falsehood can’t reach; you hear what earlier messengers heard
A foreign Qurʾan? They’d object; for believers, guidance and healing
Mūsā’s Book was disputed; every deed returns to its doer
sections.matters: It contains the surah’s prostration (38), where the Prophet ﷺ reportedly prostrated while reciting to ʿUtbah. It also answers the attack on the Qurʾan directly: nothing can corrupt it, and objections, even about its language, are only excuses.
sections.story: The Quraysh took words out of context and said an Arab reciting Arabic proves nothing. Reportedly ayah 40 was about Abū Jahl, and ayah 44 answered a taunt: either that a foreign slave taught the Prophet ﷺ, or “why not part foreign, part Arabic?”
explained: Night and day, sun and moon are His signs. So don’t prostrate to them; prostrate to Allah who made them, if you truly worship Him. If they are too proud, the angels near your Lord glorify Him night and day and never tire. Barren earth quivers and swells with rain; the One who revives it will revive the dead.

Yulḥidūna: those who twist Our ayat are not hidden from Us. Do what you want; He sees. The Qurʾan is a mighty Book: falsehood can’t reach it from front or behind. Had it been foreign, they’d complain. For believers it is guidance and healing; deniers are called from far away. Mūsā’s Book was disputed too.
teaches: Prostration belongs to Allah alone, never to anything He created.
Allah needs no one’s worship; the angels glorify Him without tiring.
The Qurʾan is protected in its words and in its meanings.
Twisting the Qurʾan’s meaning is never hidden from Allah.
The Qurʾan heals believing hearts; those who refuse it stay deaf to it.
sections.hook: Wa min āyātihi opens ayat 37 and 39. The prostration comes at the end of 38. Ayah 44 repeats fuṣṣilat āyātuhu from ayah 3 and waqr in the ears from ayah 5.

sections.title: Allah alone knows the Hour; man despairs then boasts; signs are coming
sections.meaning: Only Allah knows when the Hour comes, and every fruit and pregnancy happens with His knowledge. On that Day the idolaters disown their partners, with no escape. Man never tires of asking for good, despairs in hardship, and boasts when relief comes. Signs in the horizons and in themselves will show the Qurʾan is true.
points: The Hour, fruit, pregnancy: all in His knowledge; “Where are My partners?”
Their gods vanish; they know there is no escape
Man despairs in hardship; given relief, says “This is mine”
Blessed, he turns away; afflicted, he prays at length
If it is from Allah and you rejected it, who is more lost?
Signs in the horizons and themselves; Allah encompasses everything
sections.matters: It closes the surah on the two things the deniers doubted: the Hour and the Qurʾan. It holds up a mirror to human nature, and ends with a promise that coming signs will prove the Qurʾan true.
sections.story: No specific incident. The signs “in the horizons and in themselves” (53) are explained either as the later victories, like Badr and the conquest of Makkah, or as the wonders of the universe and the human body.
explained: Knowledge of the Hour is returned to Allah alone. No fruit leaves its sheath, no female conceives or gives birth, without His knowledge. On that Day He calls: where are My partners? They answer: we declare to You, none of us will testify to that now. Their false gods vanish, and they know there is no escape.

Man never tires of asking for good, yet despairs when hardship hits. Given relief, he says: this is mine; the Hour won’t come, and if it does I’ll get the best. Blessed, he turns away; afflicted, he prays at length. Allah will show them signs, far and within, until the truth is clear. He encompasses everything.
teaches: The timing of the Hour is Allah’s knowledge alone.
Whatever people worship besides Allah will abandon them on that Day.
Be grateful in ease and patient in hardship; don’t swing between pride and despair.
Blessings in this life are no proof of reward in the next.
Look at the world and at yourself: both point to the truth.
sections.hook: Juz 25 and page 482 both begin at ayah 47. Shahīd ends ayat 47 and 53. The last ayah has two alā: alā innahum, then alā innahu.

groups.text: Ḥā Mīm. A revelation from the Most Merciful: a Book set out clearly, an Arabic Qurʾan for people who understand.
It brings good news and warning, but most turn away, saying their hearts are covered and their ears deaf.
The Prophet ﷺ is a man given revelation: your God is One. Woe to idolaters; believers get a reward that never ends.
You deny the One who made the earth in two days? He set mountains, blessing and provision on it: four days in all.
Sky and earth obeyed willingly. He made seven heavens in two days and adorned the nearest with stars.
If they turn away, warn of a blast like ʿĀd and Thamūd’s, who rejected human messengers and wanted angels.
ʿĀd boasted, “Who is stronger than us?” A screaming wind disgraced them, and the Hereafter’s disgrace is worse.
Thamūd were shown guidance but chose blindness, so a humiliating blast took them. The God-fearing believers were saved.
Allah’s enemies are driven to the Fire. Their ears, eyes and skins testify, saying Allah made them speak.
They sinned openly, thinking Allah didn’t know much of it. That thought about their Lord ruined them.
Patient or pleading, the Fire is their home. Devilish companions had made their sins look attractive.
Deniers said, “Don’t listen, make noise.” They will taste severe punishment; the Fire is their eternal home.
In the Fire they beg to see the jinn and humans who misled them, to trample them underfoot.
Angels tell the steadfast: don’t fear or grieve. We are your allies; Paradise, with all you wish, is your welcome gift.
No one speaks better than one who calls to Allah, does good, and says, “I am one of the Muslims.”
Good and evil aren’t equal. Repel evil with better, and an enemy turns friend. Only the patient and truly fortunate achieve it.
If Satan provokes you, seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
Don’t prostrate to sun or moon, but to their Creator. If they’re too proud, the angels glorify Him tirelessly.
Dead, still earth quivers and grows when rain falls. The One who revives it will revive the dead.
Those who twist Our ayat can’t hide. Who is better: one thrown in the Fire, or one safe on Resurrection Day?
Deniers rejected the Reminder, a mighty Book falsehood can’t reach. You hear only what earlier messengers heard. Allah forgives and punishes.
A foreign Qurʾan would have drawn complaints. For believers it is guidance and healing; deniers are deaf and blind to it.
Mūsā’s Book was disputed too; judgement was delayed by Allah’s word. Good and evil return to their doer; Allah wrongs no one.
Only Allah knows the Hour, every fruit and birth. On that Day the idolaters’ partners vanish, and there is no escape.
Man never tires of asking for good, despairs in hardship, boasts after relief, and turns away until trouble returns.
If the Qurʾan is from Allah, who is more lost than its rejecters? Signs will prove it. Allah encompasses everything.

1.explain: Ḥā Mīm: separate letters whose meaning is best left to Allah, though they carry wisdom. This is one of seven surahs that open this way.

2.explain: Tanzīl: sent down from ar-Raḥmān ar-Raḥīm. Sending this Book, with its guidance, light and healing, is one of the greatest mercies of the One whose mercy covers everything.

3.explain: Fuṣṣilat āyātuhu: its ayat are set out in detail, each subject in its place, in clear Arabic. Li-qawmin yaʿlamūn: for people who understand and want to learn from it.

4.explain: Bashīr and nadhīr: good news for believers, warning for deniers. Most turned away, so they don’t hear: the words reached them, but not with a hearing that accepts.

5.explain: Akinnah: coverings over the heart; waqr: heaviness in the ears; ḥijāb: a screen, a split in religion. They said it mockingly: you follow your way, we’ll follow ours.

6.explain: Basharun mithlukum: a man like you, set apart only by revelation. Istaqīmū ilayhi: go straight to Him with sincere worship, and seek forgiveness for the slips that come. Woe to the idolaters.

7.explain: They don’t give zakah: either they don’t purify themselves with tawḥīd, or they withhold charity. Its details came later, in Madinah, but giving was commanded from the start. They also deny the Hereafter.
7.why: Reportedly, the Quraysh were known for charity and for feeding pilgrims, but cut off that help from anyone who believed in the Prophet ﷺ. This ayah was revealed about them.

8.explain: Ghayr mamnūn: never cut off and never reduced. A reward that lasts forever, and is not held over them as a favour.
8.why: Reportedly revealed about the sick, disabled and elderly: when they grow too weak for their usual worship, their reward is still written as when they were well.

9.explain: Allah rebukes the idolaters: you deny the One who made the vast earth in two days, and set up andād, rivals equal to Him? He is Lord of all the worlds.

10.explain: Rawāsī: firm mountains holding the earth steady. He blessed it and measured its aqwāt, foods suited to each land. Four days includes the first two. Sawāʾan lil-sāʾilīn: exactly, for whoever asks; or, provision for those who need it.

11.explain: Then He turned to the sky while it was dukhān, smoke or rising vapour. He told sky and earth: obey My command, willingly or unwillingly. Both answered: we come willingly.

12.explain: He completed seven heavens in two days and gave each its command. The nearest is lit with stars, for beauty and as a guard against devils listening in. This is the plan of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.

13.explain: Ṣāʿiqah: a destroying blast, like the one that wiped out ʿĀd and Thamūd. If the people of Makkah turn away after all this, they face the same.

14.explain: Messengers came to them one after another, all saying: worship only Allah. They replied that Allah would have sent angels, not men. Deniers have repeated that weak excuse ever since.

15.explain: ʿĀd were arrogant without right and boasted: who is stronger than us? Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is far stronger? Their very existence came from Him.

16.explain: Ṣarṣar: a wind that was fierce, freezing and roaring. The days were naḥisāt, ill-fated for them because of their crimes, not unlucky in themselves. A worse disgrace awaits in the Hereafter.

17.explain: Hadaynāhum: We showed Thamūd the way clearly, with the she-camel as a plain sign. They preferred blindness over guidance, so a humiliating blast seized them for what they earned.

18.explain: Allah saved Ṣāliḥ and the believers with him, because they feared Allah and avoided shirk and sin.

19.explain: Yuḥsharu aʿdāʾu Allāh: Allah’s enemies are gathered to the Fire. Yūzaʿūn: the first are held back for the last to catch up, then all are driven on together.

20.explain: When they reach it, their hearing, sight and skins testify to all they did. These three are named because most sins happen through them. Every limb says: I did this, on that day.

21.explain: They blame their skins: why testify against us? The skins answer: Allah, who gives speech to everything, made us speak. He created you the first time, and to Him you return.

22.explain: You didn’t hide your sins from your own limbs, never imagining they would testify. You assumed Allah didn’t know much of what you did.
22.why: Reportedly, three men by the Kaʿbah, from Quraysh and Thaqīf, wondered if Allah hears them. One said only if they spoke loudly; another said if He hears some, He hears all. This was revealed after the Prophet ﷺ was told.

23.explain: Ardākum: that bad assumption about your Lord destroyed you. You became losers of yourselves, your families and your religion.

24.explain: Mathwā: a permanent home. Enduring it won’t help, and yastaʿtibū, begging to be excused or sent back to make amends, won’t be accepted. The time for that has passed.

25.explain: Qayyaḍnā lahum quranāʾ: Allah assigned them devilish companions for turning from His reminder. They made the world’s pleasures attractive and the Hereafter seem far off. The sentence came true on them, as on jinn and humans before.

26.explain: Their plan: lā tasmaʿū, don’t listen to this Qurʾan, and walghaw fīhi, whistle and shout over its recitation, so you win. Their own words admit that if they listened, they would lose.

27.explain: So Allah will make them taste a severe punishment and repay them for the worst of their deeds, their shirk and disbelief.

28.explain: That is the reward of Allah’s enemies: the Fire, dār al-khuld, a home they never leave, because they rejected clear signs.

29.explain: Show us the two who misled us, of jinn and humans, to trample them into the lowest depths. The two are either all such misleaders, or Iblīs and Adam’s son who killed his brother.

30.explain: Qālū rabbunā Allāh thumma istaqāmū: they declared Allah their Lord, then stayed firm in belief and deeds. Angels descend: don’t fear what lies ahead, don’t grieve over what you left; rejoice in the promised Paradise.
30.why: Reportedly revealed about Abū Bakr: the idolaters said “Our Lord is Allah” but called the angels His daughters and intercessors, while Abū Bakr said Allah alone, with Muhammad ﷺ His servant and messenger, and stayed firm.

31.explain: Naḥnu awliyāʾukum: the angels say they guarded and helped you in this life, and will stay with you through the grave and Resurrection until Paradise. There you have whatever you desire and whatever you ask for.

32.explain: Nuzul: the welcoming meal prepared for an honoured guest. It comes from the Forgiving, who removed your sins, and the Merciful, who gave you what you hoped for.

33.explain: Aḥsanu qawlan: no one speaks better than one who calls people to Allah, practises what he calls to, and openly says, “I am one of the Muslims.” The Prophet ﷺ is foremost in this, and it covers every such caller.
33.why: Reportedly about the Prophet ﷺ; others said it was about those who call the adhān. The adhān came later in Madinah, so they are included by meaning, not as the occasion.

34.explain: Idfaʿ billatī hiya aḥsan: answer a wrong with something better. Be patient with anger, forbearing with ignorance, forgiving of harm. Then your enemy becomes like a walīy ḥamīm, a warm, close friend.
34.why: Reportedly about Abū Sufyān, once hostile to the Prophet ﷺ, who softened after becoming related to him by marriage and later accepted Islam. Another report names Abū Jahl, with the Prophet ﷺ told to bear his harm patiently.

35.explain: Mā yulaqqāhā: no one is granted this trait except those who make themselves patient, and those with a ḥaẓẓ ʿaẓīm, a great share of good in this world and the next.

36.explain: Nazgh: a push or whisper from Satan, stirring you to anger or away from good. Human enemies can be won with kindness; Satan is repelled only by seeking refuge in Allah, who hears and knows.

37.explain: Night brings rest and day brings light for work; the sun and moon order life and time. They are created and controlled, so prostrate only to their Creator. In Islam, prostration is for Allah alone.

38.explain: Fa-in istakbarū: if they’re too proud, Allah loses nothing. The angels near Him glorify Him night and day, wa hum lā yasʾamūn: never tiring. The prostration is made here, though some made it after 37.

39.explain: Khāshiʿah: the earth dry, lifeless and still. Rain falls and it ihtazzat wa rabat, stirs and swells with plants. The One who does this will bring the dead back to life; He can do anything.

40.explain: Yulḥidūna: they twist Our ayat, by denying them or forcing false meanings on them. They can’t hide. Who is better, one thrown in the Fire or one safe on Resurrection Day? “Do what you like” is a warning.
40.why: Reportedly revealed about Abū Jahl, as the one thrown into the Fire. The one who comes safe is named differently in reports: the Prophet ﷺ, Ḥamzah, ʿUthmān, ʿAmmār, or the believers in general.

41.explain: Adh-dhikr is the Qurʾan. Those who rejected it when it came will be repaid; the sentence leaves their fate unstated. Wa innahu la-kitābun ʿazīz: a mighty, honoured Book, protected from anyone who would corrupt it.

42.explain: Falsehood can’t come at it from before or behind: no devil of jinn or men can add, remove or change it, openly or through false meanings. Sent down by the Wise, the Praiseworthy.

43.explain: What the deniers say to you was said to every messenger before you, so be patient as they were. Your Lord has forgiveness for those who repent and painful punishment for those who persist.

44.explain: Had it come in a foreign tongue, they’d say: why isn’t it made clear? A foreign Book and an Arab messenger? Say: for believers it is guidance and shifāʾ, healing. Deniers hear it like someone called from far away.
44.why: Reportedly the Quraysh said the Qurʾan should be part foreign, part Arabic. Another report says they claimed Yasār, a non-Arab slave the Prophet ﷺ used to visit, was teaching him.

45.explain: Mūsā was given the Torah and people split over it, some believing, some denying, as with the Qurʾan. Had Allah not decreed a delay until the Day, judgement would have fallen at once. They are in deep, unsettling doubt.

46.explain: Good deeds benefit the doer; evil harms only the one who does it. No one carries another’s burden, and your Lord is never unjust, punishing no one without first giving proof.

47.explain: Ilayhi yuraddu ʿilmu as-sāʿah: knowing when the Hour comes belongs to Allah alone. Every fruit leaving its akmām (husks) and every birth is known to Him. On that Day, idolaters renounce the partners they claimed.

48.explain: Ḍalla ʿanhum: the idols they prayed to disappear and give no help. Ẓannū here means they are certain: there is no maḥīṣ, no way out.

49.explain: Lā yasʾamu al-insān: man never tires of asking for wealth, health and more. But when hardship touches him he becomes yaʾūs qanūṭ, losing all hope of Allah’s mercy.

50.explain: After relief, he says hādhā lī: I deserve this. He doubts the Hour, yet assumes that if it comes he’ll get the best. Allah will show deniers what they did and make them taste harsh punishment.

51.explain: Blessed, he turns aside and holds himself aloof in pride. Afflicted, he is dhū duʿāʾin ʿarīḍ, full of long prayers. The fault is not long prayer but swinging between pride and complaint.

52.explain: Say: think, if this Qurʾan really is from Allah and you rejected it, who could be more astray than someone in shiqāq baʿīd, opposition that has gone far from the truth?

53.explain: Sanurīhim āyātinā: signs in the āfāq (horizons) and in themselves, either the victories to come or the wonders of creation and the body, until it’s clear the Qurʾan is true. Isn’t Allah enough as Witness?

54.explain: Alā: truly, they doubt they will ever meet their Lord, so they don’t prepare for it. Truly, He encompasses everything in knowledge and power, so bringing the Hour is easy for Him.
